About the position
The research group DARWIN (Data, AI, and Robotics) at the NORCE Technology and digital systems division is looking for a senior scientist in a permanent 100% position with the main role of initiating and coordinating large national and EU research proposals for the research group and scientifically coordinating them as well as designing novel concepts and solutions for AI and robot deployments. The group has strong technological professional expertise in data science, AI, computer vision, machine learning, robotics, mechatronics, cybernetics, computer engineering, visual sensing, visualization, advanced maintenance and smart instrumentation.

The place of work and employment can be any NORCE location. Travelling is expected.
Work tasks
The main tasks of the position will be to drive new large national and EU research possibilities, initiate and coordinate scientific proposal writing and applications, carry out the scientific coordination and management of projects within AI and robotics. Additional tasks include carrying out technological research and development projects in collaboration with industrial partners and research organization in Norway and in Europe, as well as collaborative projects with other groups and divisions within NORCE.
Required skills, expertise and experience
• 
Scientific background: minimum master’s degree in mechanical electronics, computer science and/or mechatronics or a related scientific area, with extensive knowledge in robotics, AI and perception systems.

• 
Documented experience of at least 10 years in national and EU research funding programs with a track record on initiating scientific large national and EU project applications, writing scientific national and EU project proposals and coordinating national and EU projects is particularly relevant to the position.

• 
Industrial experience is an advantage

• 
Being and having a certified project management with IPMA, PMP or similar

• 
Proficiency in English. Knowledge of the Norwegian language is an advantage.

• 
Good team working skills while being proactive.

• 
Excellent communication and organizational skills.
We offer
• 
A good and professionally challenging working environment

• 
Exciting interdisciplinary projects together with national and international partners

• 
A nationwide network of researchers in NORCE

• 
Exciting, varied and flexible workday

• 
Interdisciplinary work in teams with experts in other fields

• 
Great opportunities for professional and personal development in a new and expansive competence environment

• 
A social and creative work environment where you have a large influence on your own workday

• 
Good pension and insurance schemes, good welfare schemes and competitive wages
How to apply
Please upload your application by pressing the application button. Your application should be written in English and must include the following:

• 
CV

• 
A cover letter with a description of your professional qualifications and motivation to apply for the position

• 
Names and contact information of two references

• 
Copy of diplomas, transcripts and relevant certificates from your higher education
Application deadline: 3 January 2027
Further information about the position can be obtained by contacting research leader Nabil Belbachir, tel. 401 08 137, or nabe@norceresearch.no.

At NORCE, we are committed to ensuring diversity, equity and inclusion. We encourage all qualified individuals to apply for available positions regardless of gender, age, disability, or ethnic background.

Candidates are expected to openly offer relevant information about themselves during the recruitment process. Furthermore, one can expect background checks to be conducted on candidates in the final phase of the recruitment process. NORCE uses external actors to carry out such background checks.

NORCE is subject to the Security Act and there are strict requirements for our employees to have a security-conscious behavior. For this position, you must satisfy the security clearance requirements for SECRET/NATO SECRET.

Further information about security clearance can be found on the National Security Authority's (NSM) website: NSM.no

About the role
At Schibsted, reliable IT services are essential to helping our employees do their best work.

We are looking for an IT Service Desk Technician to join our Service Desk team in Oslo, providing high-quality technical support to employees across our organisation, primarily in Norway and Sweden.

Our Service Desk is more than a traditional first-line support function. We resolve approximately 80% of all incoming IT requests and incidents within the team, which means you will have the opportunity to work with a wide range of technical challenges, take ownership of issues and develop your troubleshooting skills.

You will work in an international environment where customer satisfaction, technical expertise and continuous improvement are key priorities. Our IT operations follow IT Service Management (ITSM) principles and ITIL practices, with a strong focus on efficient problem-solving, knowledge sharing and improving the employee IT experience.
Your responsibilities
As an IT Service Desk Technician, your main responsibilities will include:

• 
Deliver high-quality IT support: Provide professional, friendly and solution-oriented technical support to employees through phone, email and other support channels.

• 
Troubleshoot and resolve technical issues: Investigate and resolve incidents involving computers, operating systems, applications, user accounts, access and other workplace technologies.

• 
Own incidents and service requests: Register, prioritise, investigate, document and follow up on cases in our ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Halo), taking responsibility for driving issues towards resolution.

• 
Ensure a great user experience: Communicate clearly with users, provide regular updates and manage expectations throughout the support process.

• 
Drive efficient resolution and knowledge sharing: Contribute to our high resolution rate by developing technical knowledge, documenting solutions and supporting a shift-left approach.

• 
Collaborate and continuously improve: Work closely with colleagues and other IT teams to resolve complex issues and improve processes related to Incident, Problem, Change and Knowledge Management.

• 
Manage IT equipment and suppliers: Support ordering, inventory management and distribution of IT equipment and accessories, including coordination with external suppliers.
What we're looking for
We are looking for someone who enjoys solving technical challenges, takes ownership of problems and genuinely likes helping people.

You are curious about technology, comfortable investigating unfamiliar issues and motivated by finding solutions rather than simply passing problems on to someone else.

You enjoy working in an environment where priorities can change quickly and where teamwork, knowledge sharing and customer satisfaction are essential.
Skills and knowledge
To succeed in this role, we believe you have:

• 
A good understanding of computers, operating systems, software and common workplace IT technologies.

• 
The ability to troubleshoot technical issues in a structured and logical way.

• 
Familiarity with, or an interest in learning, technologies such as Windows, macOS, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace and Microsoft Entra ID.

• 
An understanding of the importance of documenting incidents, solutions and technical information.

• 
The ability to communicate technical information clearly to users with different levels of IT knowledge.

• 
Professional proficiency in Norwegian or Swedish, as well as English, both written and spoken.
Nice to have
The following qualifications are an advantage, but not essential:

• 
Previous experience working in an IT Service Desk, IT Support or similar technical support role.

• 
Around two years of relevant technical experience or education.

• 
Experience working with ITSM platforms such as ServiceNow or Halo.

• 
Knowledge of ITIL principles and IT Service Management processes.

• 
Relevant IT certifications or technical training.

• 
Experience with IT equipment management, inventory control or supplier coordination.

• 
Experience with AI tools and technologies, particularly using AI to improve IT support, automate tasks, enhance troubleshooting or streamline workflows.

We value practical skills, curiosity and a willingness to learn. You do not need to meet every preferred qualification to be considered for the role.
Who you are
We believe the following qualities will help you succeed:

• 
Customer oriented: You enjoy helping others, understand their needs and take pride in delivering excellent service.

• 
Problem-solving: You approach technical challenges with curiosity, persistence and a structured mindset, taking responsibility for finding solutions.

• 
Communication: You explain technical issues clearly, listen actively and keep users informed throughout the support process.

• 
Adaptable: You are comfortable handling changing priorities, learning new technologies and working in a dynamic IT environment.

• 
Collaborative: You enjoy sharing knowledge, supporting colleagues and contributing to a positive and supportive team environment.
Why join us?
You will join a Service Desk team in Oslo where technical problem-solving, collaboration and high-quality service go hand in hand.

Unlike traditional first-line support roles, our team handles and resolves the majority of incoming IT issues, giving you the opportunity to work with a broad range of technologies and technical challenges.

You will support colleagues across Norway and Sweden, work with modern workplace technologies and contribute to continuously improving how IT services are delivered.

We believe great IT support is about more than fixing technical problems. It is about taking ownership, building trust and making people's working lives easier.

About the position
We invite applications for a full time permanent position as Associate Professor in Clincal Pharmacy at the Section for Pharmaceutics and Social Pharmacy, Department of Pharmacy, University of Oslo.
About the Department and what we are looking for in this position
The Department of Pharmacy at the University of Oslo is seeking a highly motivated, dynamic, and innovative researcher with strong collaborative and educational skills. The Department has a strong interdisciplinary environment that covers the key areas of the pharmaceutical field. Cutting-edge research, extensive national and international collaboration, and an integrated Master’s programme in Pharmacy position the Department as a key contributor to the development of pharmacy in Norway. We place strong emphasis on collaboration with the healthcare sector, regulatory authorities, as well as the pharmaceutical industry. The Section for Pharmaceutics and Social pharmacy is one of the three sections at the Department of Pharmacy and is comprised of strong research groups specializing in clinical pharmacy, as well as pharmacoepidemiology and pharmaceutics. The section offers an active and dynamic academic environment, ideal for ambitious researchers. The research environment (Clinical pharmacy - Department of Pharmacy) focuses on patient safety, medication use, and continuity of care, supported by methodological expertise spanning from qualitative studies to randomised trials, as well as health care innovation and strong collaboration with healthcare partners in the Oslo region.
 
The life science environment in the Oslo region is developing steadily, supported by collaboration between the pharmaceutical sector, the university hospital and hospital pharmacy, and academic institutions. Oslo Science City and the new Life Science Building are central initiatives contributing to this development. The Department of Pharmacy is relocating to the new Life Science Building in 2026 (Life Science building- UiO:Livsvitenskap). This move will provide modern facilities designed to strengthen research, teaching, and collaboration across the health and life science disciplines at the University of Oslo. 

The ideal candidate will play an important role in shaping the department’s activities in the new Life Science Building by contributing to the development of pharmaceutical sciences within a strong interdisciplinary environment. In particular, the candidate is expected to strengthen research and academic activity to contribute to the research group’s collaboration with healthcare partners and other research groups. Documented experience with interdisciplinary work and international cooperation is highly desirable.

The successful candidate should have documented independent research experience in addition to the PhD degree with publications in international peer review journals. Furthermore, the candidate should have a documented history of securing significant external funding, or at least strong funding application efforts.  
Your main tasks will be
• Teaching and supervision, mainly in social pharmacy, at all levels of the five-years study program in pharmacy, including master- and PhD. 
• Course leadership for the main course in social pharmacy at the undergraduate program.
• Initiating and conducting high quality research within the research group’s focus areas, including contributing to external funding.
• Contributing to the development of a strong and sustainable research group.
• Carrying out examination related duties and contributing to academic administration as required. More information about the position
Applicants must document academic qualifications in their field, equivalent to an Associate professor position. The successful applicant must be able to teach at all levels and to supervise Master and PhD students. The successful applicant may furthermore be required to take on other teaching duties and administrative tasks, by request from the Department or the Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences. 
What skills are important in this role?
Required qualifications that must be documented in the application::

• The successful applicant must have completed a PhD preferably in clinical or social pharmacy and have a strong scientific track record within the area.
• Master’s degree in pharmacy or equivalent must be formally documented. 
• Scientific qualifications will play a major role, with main emphasis placed on research output from the last five years. 
• Documented potential for further acquisition of external funding.
• Documented knowledge of Scandinavian pharmaceutical practice and traditions.
• Pedagogical qualifications and teaching and supervision experience at all levels will be an important factor in the evaluation process and should be well documented in a teaching portfolio. The applicant should describe her/his qualifications in view of the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL) framework which includes:
• Focus on student learning
• A clear development over time
• A researching approach
• A collegial attitude and practice
• The successful candidate who at the time of appointment cannot document sufficient teaching qualifications (minimum formal requirement is a 200 hours pedagogical programme) will be required to obtain such qualifications within a two-year period.
• Teaching in the pharmacy program is conducted primarily in Norwegian. Applicants are required to document proficiency in Norwegian at a minimum level of B2. The successful candidate must also demonstrate strong written and oral communication skills in Norwegian, or another Scandinavian language, in relevant assessment settings such as a trial lecture and interview.
Desired qualifications:

• Candidates should be able to establish, lead and conduct research projects, also as a collaborator. A track record in scientific and administrative management is an advantage.
• An international research network and documented experience with international collaboration.
• Ability to contribute to the development of a strong and sustainable research group.
• Experience with working within the European healthcare setting, for example pharmacy, or with interprofessional collaboration
• The person appointed will be requested to take on some administrative duties. Hence such experience will be an advantage.
• Experience with independent teaching responsibilities and with the development of study programmes.
• Experience with planning and conducting of clinical trials as well as regulatory experience in drug development. What are we looking for in you?
• Strong communication skills with students and colleagues.
• Ability to create and contribute to a well-functioning, inclusive, supporting and productive research environment
• Strong networking skills, ability to collaborate and conduct scientific leadership
• Ability to cooperate and communicate well with other members of staff
The successful candidate is expected to have an international profile in relation to the criteria outlined above. Selection for this position will be based on academic excellence and the candidate’s fit within the research group and the group’s research profile. In addition, pedagogical competence and personal suitability for contributing to a collaborative and supportive academic environment will form part of the overall assessment.
We can offer you

• Opportunities for academic leadership and career development.
• Committed colleagues in a good working environment.

About the project
Globally, electricity demand is increasing and expected to increase in the coming years, supported by higher consumption from industrial actors, increasing electrification and integration of electric vehicles, data centers and other electrical sources. The electrical grid is getting increasingly strained due to the increased load, which needs to handle the power-intense appliances, while also needing to enable more renewable energy production into the power system. In both the EU and Norway, the ageing distribution grid is expected to have challenges in the future year due to the energy transition, needing investments and reinforcements to prevent critical situations such as voltage issues and bottlenecks in the grid. To combat these issues due to long lead time on investments and immature replacement situations, flexibility is seen as a vital part to enable more active operation of the electrical grid to prolong secure operational conditions. Ensuring local flexible resources in local distributional grids can be enabled for grid support and be integrated as part of the operational solutions without impacting their own operational situations to a large degree will be key to understanding and assessing the potential available. 

The objective of this PhD project is to develop new knowledge, models, methods, and analytical insights into how flexible resources can be utilized to provide grid support to the local distribution grid, while also participating in defined electrical markets and balancing markets. The flexible resources aim to maximize their revenues through different market options, and the consequences this will have on the local distribution grid. How upholding local conditions can be performed will be important to enable value-stacking grid services in an efficient manner. Local distributional systems operators (DSOs) might not have defined specific local markets for grid support, and how this service impacts other revenue streams and how TSO-DSO-coordination impacts operations will need to be analyzed. The project will focus on how these local conditions can be accounted for in long-term operational planning by the flexible provider, while also being accounted for during short-term operational decisions and reserve market activation sequences. Use of both active and reactive power to enable efficient grid operations will be a key aspect to approach this work.

The PhD candidate will develop and apply optimization-based models that capture the dynamics of the electricity grid and different flexible providers in the distributional grid (for instance, but not limited to batteries, EV parking lots, industrial demand, etc.). Key focus will be put into methods that can simplify grid information, to reduce the need for grid-sensitive information during operational planning and operation. Regulatory aspects and TSO-DSO coordination schemes will also need to be addressed and investigated as part of the project.

Project description
The position is funded by the Research Council of Norway through the Researcher Project for Early Career Scientists (FRIPRO) “APExModel: Addressing Antimicrobial Peptides by Integrating Experiments into Modelling” and lead by Henrique Musseli Cezar. 

Antimicrobial resistance is a critical global health crisis, and new drugs are urgently needed. 

APExModel will establish a set of experimentally-grounded design principles that can aid the development of safer and more effective AMPs. This will be done by developing and applying a new computational framework that integrates experimental data into simulations. The project will also provide: 1) better understanding the molecular mechanisms that govern how AMPs self-assemble in solution, a key factor for their stability and activity; 2) a novel simulation methodology that can accurately model AMPs interacting with cell membranes by using experimental small-angle scattering data to guide the simulations; and 3) insights on the action mechanisms of different AMPs and how they disrupt bacterial membranes.

The most critical R&D challenge is the development of this new simulation methodology. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provide access to dynamics at atomic resolution, but limitations in simulation timescale and accuracy may compromise the agreement with experiments. Current integrative approaches are limited to systems with spherical symmetry and cannot adequately model the flat, patch-like membrane used in most MD simulations of AMP-membrane studies. This project will overcome this limitation, adding a capability that is currently missing in the field.

Combining expertise from chemistry, pharmacy, and physics, this interdisciplinary project will produce a new open-source simulation tool and the fundamental knowledge required to establish design principles for AMPs.

You’ll take ownership of a portfolio of key customers, getting to know their businesses and helping them find the right solutions as their needs develop.

Alongside renewals and commercial discussions, you’ll initiate conversations, reach new stakeholders and uncover opportunities within existing customers and selected potential accounts.

Software development is changing quickly. Your curiosity about how customers work, what alternatives they consider and where we can make a difference will help shape our approach.

Upsell scope and products, prepare proposals and lead commercial and legal negotiations.

•

Build and manage your sales pipeline, with clear priorities and next steps.

• 
Work with legal, product, marketing, and technical colleagues, sharing customer insights along the way.

You enjoy building relationships and making things happen. You’re comfortable starting conversations, asking thoughtful questions and following through when an opportunity takes time.

Good commercial judgement and experience working with several stakeholders in a sales process.

Strong written and spoken English.

A structured approach to customers, opportunities and follow-up.

You’ll work with international customers and have a real say in how we develop our approach to sales.

Helpful colleagues who share their knowledge and make time to support you.

• 
Trust and flexibility to take ownership of your work.

• 
Room to grow your skills and bring new approaches into the team.

A warm, informal culture with space for ambition and humour.

Life outside work, supported by flexible working hours.

Join us in Vik, Sogndal or Bergen, with occasional customer visits when relevant.
